newsitem.title: USA: Georgia economic indicators rise in May.
newsitem.headline: Georgia economic indicators rise in May.

text.p: Georgia's Composite Index of Leading Indicators rose in May for the ninth time in 12 months, a signal that the state's economy is expected to remain healthy, state Labor Commissioner David Poythress said.
Leading indicators, designed to forecast economic activity three to six months ahead, rose 0.51 point to 149.79 on a 1988 base of 100.
The state's Composite Index of Coincident Indicators, which measures current economic conditions, rose 0.29 point to 146.41.

The gains were fueled by declining unemployment claims, an increase in new corporate charters and continuing strength in the manufacturing workweek. New motor vehicle sales and residential construction permits were down.
Nonfarm employment grew by 3,000 during the month to 3.58 million. That was an increase of 60,000, or 1.70 percent over May 1996.

State revenue collections totalled $878.4 million, up 1.4 percent from April and up 2.52 percent from May 1996. Sales tax revenues dipped to $330.4 million, down 0.66 percent from April and down 4.06 percent from May 1996.
